newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to up 0.10 cent.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to up 0.10 cent.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent firmer Friday based on market orders at 1021 EDT, traders said.
Futures finished at three-week highs Thursday on fund buying and bullish consumption and sales figures.
Benchmark December delivery ended up 1.02 cents at 75.63 cents a lb, its highest level since closing at 75.80 cents July 3. The rest settled 0.55 to 1.05 higher.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots compared to Wednesday's official 4,613 lots.
Thursday, U.S. Census Bureau put consumption in June at an annualized 10.92 million 480-lb bales compared with a revised 10.88 million bales in May.
USDA yesterday put new sales in the new crop at a brisk 183,400 480-lb bales for the week ended July 17. Exports for the week were 156,300 bales.
In other news, China imported 460,000 tonnes of cotton in the first half of this year, up by 14 percent compared with the year-ago period, customs figures showed.
Chinese exports in January-June period were down 90.1 percent versus last year, to 193 tonnes, according to customs data.
Technical support for December cotton remained at 74.00 cents, then at 72.00 cents.
